# About you

## Stance
Use only the athlete's volunteered information and Tempo-derived training context. Coach training decisions; do not diagnose medical conditions or prescribe treatment. If something sounds medical or outside coaching, urge the athlete to seek a qualified professional and keep training conservative.

## Goal
You are training for the Lakeshore Marathon on Sun Nov 15, aiming for 3:30. This will be your fourth marathon, and your personal best is 3:41 from two years ago.

## Schedule
You run five days a week: Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat and Sun. Mon and Fri are fixed rest days because of work travel.

Weekday runs are early, around 6am before work, capped near an hour. Saturday is an easy hour and Sunday is the long run.

Typical volume is 6 to 7 hours a week, with more on long-run weeks.

## Running history
You have run three marathons already, best 3:41. You eased off in June and have built back to about 30 miles a week through July.

Recent weeks show four easy runs of roughly 5 to 6 miles and a long run of about 10.8 miles on Sun Aug 2.

## Injuries and constraints
You are healthy right now. You had shin splints in your first marathon block, so you prefer to ramp mileage up carefully.

Work travel takes you away about one week in six. Mon and Fri rest days cannot move.

## Preferences
You train mostly on flat paved loops and a canal path, with one hillier route on Thursdays. You want easy days to be properly easy and you are happy to work hard on quality days.

You like to know why a session is in the plan. Shoes: Brooks Ghost 16 for daily miles, Saucony Endorphin Speed 4 for workouts.

## Current status
You are at about 30 miles a week with a long run near 11 miles. Units are miles. Heart rate zones are set custom, with easy running in 112 – 150 bpm.

recentHistory.analysis:
## Why this shape

Last week was the first full load since the Achilles flare and it held together: tempo at 7:35/mi, long run at 9:18/mi with only +8.8 bpm drift, and no body-check flags. That earns a careful step up, not a leap. Seven weeks to race day means two more build weeks, then a peak block, then taper.

## The quality day

Thursday is 2 x 2 miles at marathon pace with a 3-minute jog between. That is a longer continuous touch of 8:00/mi than the three Thursday tempo miles you ran last week, but still well short of the 8-mile MP session from early September. Stay on the flat canal loop, not the Thursday hills — pace changes and climbs are what loaded the tendon last time.

## The long run

Fourteen miles Sunday with the last 2 at marathon pace. This is the first MP-on-tired-legs rep since the Achilles episode, kept deliberately short so you finish wanting more. If anything whispers in the tendon during the first 10 miles, drop the MP finish and jog it home — no points for toughing it out this far from the race.

## Guardrails

Keep the heel drops going daily, keep the Ghost 16 for everything except Thursday, and keep easy days honest (HR under 150). Wednesday drifted to 13.6% Z3 last week — fine, but let's keep it Z2 this week with Thursday getting harder.

recentHistory.analysis:
## Where we are

You lost about a week of load but the aerobic base is intact. Easy pace is still 9:20 – 9:30/mi at HR 142 – 143, and the Sunday long run drifted a reasonable +8 bpm over 8 miles. That is a healthy platform to build from with eight weeks until Lakeshore.

## Why this shape

The physio cleared one short tempo, so Thursday is deliberately small: a 2-mile tempo at 8:15 – 8:25/mi, not marathon pace. Short enough to test the Achilles under load, long enough to feel like a workout. If morning stiffness returns at any point before Thursday, swap it for an easy 5.

The long run moves back to 12 miles at pure easy effort. No marathon pace finish this week — we need two clean weeks of tempo and long run before layering goal pace on tired legs again. If Sunday goes well, the week of Sep 28 goes to 14 and we start reintroducing MP work the week after.

## Easy running

Three of the four easy runs last week crept toward 9:17 – 9:20/mi. That is sharper than it needs to be in a rebuild week. Open every run at 10:00/mi for the first mile and let HR, not pace, decide the rest.

## Keep doing

Twice-daily heel drops, the two short strength sessions, and the pre-run stiffness check. If first-mile stiffness ever rises above a 3/10 or sharpens with pace, stop the run and tell me — that is the signal the physio gave you, and it is the right one.

recentHistory.analysis:
## Why this shape

You stopped Thursday's session because the Achilles got sharper with pace, and Saturday it was stiff for a mile before settling. That is the classic early-warning pattern and the right response is a short, soft week — not a lost block. The race is nine weeks out and your aerobic base is in good shape, so losing a sharpening week costs you nothing.

Quality is out this week. Pace changes and push-off load the Achilles the most, and that is exactly what provoked it. We hold easy aerobic running at flat routes only, and skip the Thursday hill loop.

## How to run this week

Use a simple traffic-light rule each day. Pain under 2/10 that eases in the first mile and does not get worse while running: go. Pain 3/10 or climbing during the run: stop and walk home. Any sharp pain, swelling, or morning limp: do not run and get it looked at.

Shoes stay in the Ghost 16 all week — more stack, less heel drop stress than the Speed 4. Skip calf raises and anything that loads the Achilles hard until a professional clears you. Short, gentle walking is fine and helpful.

## What's next

If the Achilles settles cleanly by Sunday, next week we rebuild to a normal easy week and then layer quality back in the week after. If it is still grumbling, we hold easy or cross-train longer. Nine weeks is enough runway to protect this and still run 3:30 — pushing through it now is what turns a tight tendon into a six-week problem.

recentHistory.analysis:
## Why a cutback now

You went from 33.7 miles to 44.4 in a single step, with a 16-mile long run that finished at marathon pace. That is a lot of new load in one week, and the +13.4 bpm drift on Sunday tells me the back half cost more than the pace suggests. A small pullback now protects the gains and keeps the shins quiet.

## What I like

Marathon pace on Thursday sat at 7:58 – 8:01/mi with an average HR of 153 and you called it a 6/10. That is the first clean read we have had on goal pace, and the fact that you felt controlled is the sentence I care about most. Easy pace has drifted from 9:43 to 9:30 at the same 144 HR, which is honest aerobic progress.

## What this week does

Mileage lands near 38 with the long run at 14 and no marathon-pace finish. Thursday is four MP miles broken into reps so you touch 8:00/mi again without stacking two hard long efforts back to back. If next Sunday feels crisp, the week after we go back up — likely 16 again, this time with a longer MP block built in.

## Easy running

The two easy days drifted into Z3 last week (Wed 19% Z3, long run 19% Z3). That is where cutback weeks earn their keep. Start the first mile at 10:00/mi or slower on every easy day and let HR, not pace, set the ceiling.
